The natural gas feedstock (Stream 1), delivered by pipeline, is first sent to a sulfur guard unit that uses a ZnO catalyst to remove methanethiol, which can poison the reforming catalysts. Next, the desulfurized natural gas (Stream 2) is mixed with steam (Stream 3) at a steam-to- carbon molar ratio of 1.56. The mixture is sent to the prereformer where hydrocarbons are reformed over a catalyst to produce a partially-reformed gas stream (Stream 4). Ambient air (Stream 5) enters the air separation unit, which produces O (Stream 6) for the autothermal 2 reformer unit and N (Stream 7) for ammonia synthesis. The autothermal reformer completes 2 the reforming process to produce syngas. The hot syngas (Stream 8) is sent to syngas coolers, which cool the syngas from 1,093 °C (2,000 °F) to 204 °C (400 °F) while producing steam. The cooled syngas (Stream 9) is then sent through a series of three water gas shift reactors in which carbon monoxide and water are converted to additional H and CO . As carbon oxides and water need to be removed prior to 2 2 the ammonia synthesis loop due to their ability to poison the catalyst, the shifted syngas (Stream 10) is sent to the Shell ADIP-Ultra pre-combustion CO capture system that removes 99 2 percent of the CO in the syngas. The ADIP-Ultra unit produces low-pressure (Stream 11) and 2 medium-pressure (Stream 12) streams containing CO that are dried and compressed to 15.3 2 MPa (2,214.7 psia) (Stream 25). The remaining carbon oxides in the gas stream (Stream 13) are removed via the pressure swing adsorber. The off-gas from the pressure swing adsorber (Stream 15) is sent to the H recovery membrane, which recovers additional H for ammonia synthesis. 2 2 The high-purity H stream (Stream 14) is mixed with N from the air separation unit, and it is 2 2 compressed to 13.8 MPa (2,000 psia) (Stream 16) before entering the ammonia synthesis loop. The NH formed is cooled and condensed then separated via flash tanks within the ammonia 3 synthesis loop and, due to the low single-pass conversion of about 20 percent, the unreacted components are recycled back to the reactor. The purged stream (Stream 17), which is necessary to prevent the buildup of argon, nitrogen, methane, and higher hydrocarbons in the synthesis loop, is sent through a series of H recovery membranes, which recover H (Stream 18) 2 2 70 COMPARISON OF COMMERCIAL, STATE-OF-THE-ART, FOSSIL-BASED AMMONIA PRODUCTION to be recycled back to the H /N compressor. The ammonia-rich stream exiting the synthesis 2 2 loop is further purified via flash separation and the impurities go through a water wash step that recovers additional NH product. The ammonia product (Stream 19) is produced at a 3 temperature of -33 °C (-27 °F), pressure of 0.14 MPa (20 psia), and purity of 99.6 wt% and is ready for storage in an atmospheric insulated cylindrical tank.
